title: Tengo frío or estoy cansado?
note: Mix the two in one drill: learners say *estoy hambre and *tengo cansado. Frame: Tengo hambre / sed / sueño / frío (nouns) vs Estoy cansado / enfermo / aburrido (adjectives).

title: "There is" or "it's there"?
muy or mucho?

forms.en: There are a lot of people.

title: He ido vs fui: experience vs a dated past
es:
¿Has estado en Cartagena?
Sí, fui el año pasado.
en:
Have you been to Cartagena?
Yes, I went last year.

forms.es:
¿Has estado en Cartagena?
Sí, fui el año pasado.
forms.en:
Have you been to Cartagena?
Yes, I went last year.
I went to the bank today.

forms.es: Todavía no he ido a Leticia.
forms.en: I haven't been to Leticia yet.

note: LatAm: preterite for any finished event including today (Hoy fui al banco); perfecto for experience/'ever' and 'not yet' (¿Has ido a Cartagena? Todavía no he ido). Drop the old lesson's Peninsular 'hoy he…' framing.

title: Did or have done? Hoy fui… vs ¿Has ido alguna vez?
note: The core LatAm rule: finished = preterite, even today; perfecto only for experience / not yet.
en: I went to the bank today.

forms.en: I went to the bank today.
Have you ever been to Leticia?

title: Know: sé or conozco?
es: Conozco a Vale, pero no sé dónde vive.

title: Can: sé nadar or puedo nadar?
es: Sé nadar, pero hoy no puedo.

title: Me lavo las manos, not *mis manos
note: With body parts and clothes the pronoun says whose; the noun takes the article. Possessives stay for things that aren't 'part of you' or for contrast.

title: English -ing: estudiar or estudiando?
note: -ing as a noun (subject/object, after prepositions and gustar) = infinitive: Me gusta nadar, Antes de salir, Fumar es malo. Only 'be doing' = estar + gerund.

title: trabajo or estoy trabajando?
Perdón, disculpe or lo siento?
note: Lo siento for bumping into someone sounds heavy; perdón for bad news sounds dismissive. Frame: Perdón / Disculpe (small bump, getting past, attention) vs Lo siento (real harm, sympathy) vs Siento + infinitive (naming the thing).

title: Me too: yo también or a mí también?
en:
I live in Bogotá.
Me too.

forms.en:
I live in Bogotá.
Me too.

forms.es:
Me encanta el ajiaco.
A mí también.

No me gusta el café.
A mí tampoco.
forms.en:
I don't like coffee.
Me neither.

note: Echo the shape of the statement: Trabajo aquí → Yo también; Me gusta → A mí también; No me gusta → A mí tampoco. *Yo también after me gusta is a top A1 error.

title: Ask for or ask: pedir or preguntar?
What happened or what it was like? (the two pasts)
note: Big five: re-drilled every review day from u12 to C1.

title: Ven vs venga: telling a friend vs a stranger
en: Come and sit down. (to a friend)

forms.en: Come and sit down. (to a friend)

note: tú = él-form of the present (habla, come) + 8 irregulars; usted swaps the vowel (hable, coma). In Bogotá usted is common even among friends — choose by the relationship already in use. No vosotros forms.

title: tú or usted?
note: Colombia: usted is common even among friends and family; follow the other person.
en: Do you want anything? (to a friend)

forms.en: Do you want anything? (to a friend)

title: lo, la or le?
note: Standard LatAm: lo/la for the thing or person, le for to/for whom. No leísmo.

title: Three que's: ¿qué?, el que relative, creo que

forms.es: El libro que leo es muy bueno.
forms.en: The book I'm reading is very good.

note: Accent only on the question/exclamation word (¿Qué…?, No sé qué…, ¡Qué…!); relative que (el libro que leo) and conjunction que (creo que…) carry none and are never dropped.

title: Para or porque?
es: Estudio español para trabajar aquí (purpose, + infinitive) vs Estudio español porque quiero trabajar aquí (reason, + clause).
en: I study Spanish to work here vs because I want to work here.
note: Learners use porque for both and lose the difference; also *para quiero.

title: es or está with a description?
note: Big five.

title: Where it is or where it takes place?

forms.es: La fiesta es en el café.
forms.en: The party is at the café.

title: Estoy cansada vs he estado cansada

forms.es: He estado cansada toda la semana.
forms.en: I've been tired all week. (a woman speaking)

note: Participle after estar/ser/noun agrees like an adjective (cansada, cerradas); after haber it never changes (he cerrado las ventanas).

title: Le doy el libro → se lo doy (never *le lo)
es: Le doy el libro. → Se lo doy.
en: I give him the book. → I give it to him.
note: le/les becomes se before lo/la/los/las; the pair stays together (se lo voy a dar / voy a dárselo).

title: La fiesta es en… vs la casa está en…
es: La fiesta es en mi casa.
en: The party is at my place.

forms.es: La fiesta es en mi casa.
forms.en: The party is at my place.

note: Events take place → ser; people and things are located → estar. ¿Dónde es la fiesta? / ¿Dónde está tu casa?

title: por or para?
note: Big five; re-drilled after g:por-para-2.

title: Mi vs mío: my book vs a friend of mine
note: mi/tu/su before the noun, never alone; mío/tuyo/suyo after the noun, after ser, or with el/la to stand alone. *es mi, *el mi libro.

title: Estará en casa: will be or probably is?

forms.es:
¿Dónde está Vale?
Estará en el trabajo.
forms.en:
Where's Vale?
She's probably at work.

note: Same form, two times: Mañana estará en casa (prediction) vs No contesta… estará dormido (guess about now). Time words decide.

title: voy a llamar or llamaré?
en: I'm going to call you tomorrow.

forms.en: I'm going to call you tomorrow.

title: Si llueve, not *si lloverá
en: If it rains, I won't go.

forms.en: If it rains, I won't go.
If I have time, I'll go.

note: Real conditions: si + present always; the future (or imperative / present) goes only in the other half: Si tengo tiempo, iré. Frame: si + present, never si + future: *Si lloverá, no iré.

title: quiero ir or quiero que vayas?
Three se's: se levanta, se conocieron, se vende
note: Reflexive (to oneself), reciprocal (to each other, plural), impersonal (nobody in particular). Ask: one person, two acting on each other, or no one named?

title: Hace dos años or desde hace dos años?

forms.es: Vivo aquí desde hace dos años.
forms.en: I've been living here for two years.

forms.es: Hace dos años que vivo aquí.
forms.en: I've been living here for two years.

note: *Vivo aquí hace dos años is the typical slip. Standard Spanish keeps hace invariable (hace dos años, not *hacen). Frame: hace + time (a point in the past) vs desde hace + time / hace + time + que (still going)

title: pero or sino?
es: No es caro, pero es malo.
en: It's not expensive, but it's bad.

forms.es: No es caro, pero es malo.
forms.en: It's not expensive, but it's bad.

title: Tan vs tanto: as tall as, as much as

forms.en: She has as much patience as you.
He works as much as I do.

note: tan + adjective/adverb (invariable); tanto/a/os/as + noun (agrees); verb + tanto como (invariable). *tan gente, *tanto alto.

title: para + verb or para que?

forms.en: I came so that you can help me.

title: creo que es or no creo que sea?
note: Big five (mood).

title: es verdad que or es bueno que?
Guessing vs doubting: supongo que llega vs dudo que llegue
note: Both uncertain; only doubt takes the subjunctive.

title: Don't mind or approve: me da igual, me parece bien

forms.es:
¿Vamos al cine o a cenar?
Me da igual.
forms.en:
Shall we go to the cinema or out for dinner?
I don't mind.

forms.es:
¿Te parece bien si invito a Vale?
Sí, me parece bien.
forms.en:
Is it OK with you if I invite Vale?
Yes, that's fine by me.

note: Indifference can sound dismissive where approval is expected.

title: Taking a side vs agreeing with a claim
es: Estoy a favor de la ciclovía.
en: I'm in favour of the bike lane.

forms.es: Estoy a favor de la ciclovía.
forms.en: I'm in favour of the bike lane.

forms.es: No estoy de acuerdo con lo que dijiste.
forms.en: I don't agree with what you said.

title: Guessing now or guessing then: estará or estaría?
Gradable vs absolute: me molesta un poco vs no soporto
es: Me molesta un poco que llegue tarde.
en: It bothers me a bit that he arrives late.

forms.es: Me molesta un poco que llegue tarde.
forms.en: It bothers me a bit that he arrives late.
I can't stand it when people shout at me.

note: Molestar grades (un poco, muchísimo); odiar / no soportar do not. Frame: Me molesta un poco que… / No soporto que…

title: Sad vs mad: me da pena que vs me da rabia que
es: Me da pena que se vaya.
en: It makes me sad that she's leaving.

forms.es: Me da pena que se vaya.
forms.en: It makes me sad that she's leaving.

forms.es: Me da rabia que se vaya sin avisar.
forms.en: It makes me mad that she's leaving without telling anyone.

note: Same frame, opposite feeling; mixed practice stops learners defaulting to one.

title: voy or me voy? (and other se pairs)
fue or había sido?

forms.es: Cuando llegué, ya se había ido.
forms.en: When I arrived, he had already left.

title: cuando llego or cuando llegue?
en: Whenever I arrive, I call him.

forms.en: Whenever I arrive, I call him.
When I get there, I'll call him.

title: Suggesting with indicative vs proposing with subjunctive
note: Si never takes the present subjunctive.

title: Still doing it or stopped? sigo yendo or dejé de ir
en: I still go to the gym.

forms.en: I still go to the gym.
I stopped going to the gym.
Are you still working at the café?

forms.es: Dejé de fumar hace un año.
forms.en: I stopped smoking a year ago.

note: Mixed practice: same event, opposite ends. Gerund after seguir, de + infinitive after dejar. Frame: seguir + gerund; dejar de + infinitive

title: que tiene or que tenga?
es: Busco el local que tiene cocina.
en: I'm looking for the place that has a kitchen.

forms.es: Busco el local que tiene cocina.
forms.en: I'm looking for the place that has a kitchen.

forms.es: Busco un local que tenga cocina.
forms.en: I'm looking for a place that has a kitchen.

title: How big it is or whether it fits: mide, cabe
en: The table is two metres long.

forms.en: The table is two metres long.

forms.es: La mesa no cabe en la cocina.
forms.en: The table doesn't fit in the kitchen.
Does it fit in the car?

note: Measurement fact vs fit in a specific space.

title: Le permito ir vs le permito que vaya
note: Both correct; mixed practice on choosing and forming either.

title: tengo que, debo or debería?
Más que vs más de lo que

forms.es: Gana más de lo que dice.
forms.en: He earns more than he says.

note: Noun/pronoun → que; clause → de lo que.

title: Según vs depende de
es:
¿A qué hora sales del trabajo?
Según el día.
en:
What time do you leave work?
Depending on the day.

forms.es:
¿A qué hora sales del trabajo?
Según el día.
forms.en:
What time do you leave work?
Depending on the day.

note: según needs no verb and no de; depender always takes de (*depende según).

title: Taking long or being late: se demoró, llegó tarde
es: El bus se demoró una hora.

forms.es: El bus se demoró una hora.
Me demoré mucho en encontrar la casa.
forms.en: It took me ages to find the house.

forms.es: ¿Cuánto te demoras en llegar al trabajo?
forms.en: How long does it take you to get to work?

note: Duration vs lateness against a schedule; English 'late' covers both.

title: dice que vienes or dice que vengas?
fue cerrado or estaba cerrado?
es: El café fue cerrado por la alcaldía.
en: The café was closed down by the council.

forms.es: El café fue cerrado por la alcaldía.
forms.en: The café was closed down by the council.

title: Por + verb (because) vs para + verb (in order to)
en: He was fined for driving fast.

forms.en: He was fined for driving fast.

forms.es: Manejó rápido para llegar a tiempo.
forms.en: He drove fast to get there on time.
He was fired for being late.
He got up early to get there early.

note: por looks back at a cause, para forward to a goal: Lo despidieron por llegar tarde / Madrugó para llegar temprano.

title: Realise or find out: me di cuenta, me enteré
es: Me di cuenta de que había perdido las llaves.
en: I realised I'd lost my keys.

forms.es: Me di cuenta de que había perdido las llaves.
forms.en: I realised I'd lost my keys.

forms.es: Me enteré de que Vale se va.
No me di cuenta de la hora.

note: Realising by yourself vs being told; English 'realise' is often over-used for both.

title: Where events are vs where things are: es en vs está en
es: La fiesta es en el salón.
en: The party is in the hall.

forms.es: La fiesta es en el salón.
forms.en: The party is in the hall.

forms.es: El salón está en el segundo piso.
forms.en: The hall is on the second floor.

note: Event → ser; place/thing → estar.

title: Thanks to, because of or due to: gracias a, por culpa de, debido a
es: Gracias a la lluvia, las plantas están verdes.
en: Thanks to the rain, the plants are green.

forms.es: Gracias a la lluvia, las plantas están verdes.
forms.en: Thanks to the rain, the plants are green.

forms.es: Por culpa de la lluvia, cancelaron el partido.
forms.en: Because of the rain, they called off the match.

forms.es: Debido a la lluvia, el vuelo está retrasado.
forms.en: Due to the rain, the flight is delayed.

note: Choose by value: positive, negative or neutral.

title: Hard to do: "esto es difícil de hacer" vs "es difícil hacer esto"
es: Este texto es difícil de entender.
en: This text is hard to understand.

forms.es: Este texto es difícil de entender.
forms.en: This text is hard to understand.
It's hard to understand this text.

note: de only when the thing is the subject.

title: si tengo or si tuviera?
en: If I have time, I'll go.

forms.en: If I have time, I'll go.
If I had time, I'd go.

title: que venga or que viniera?
Do you mind if… vs would you mind if…
en: Do you mind if I open the window?

forms.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
Would you mind if I opened the window?

title: Not necessary vs not allowed: no hace falta que vs está prohibido que

forms.en: You're not allowed to go in.

note: English 'you don't have to' vs 'you mustn't' maps onto this.

title: Advice or reproach: deberías hacerlo vs deberías haberlo hecho
note: Classic slip: simple infinitive for something already done.

title: Becoming: se hizo rico or llegó a ser rico
note: Llegar a ser = gradual achievement; hacerse = effort/choice; volverse = change of character; ponerse = temporary.

title: Been doing or been without: llevo un año estudiando, llevo un año sin estudiar
en: I've been studying Spanish for a year.

forms.en: I've been studying Spanish for a year.
I haven't studied for a year.
I haven't smoked for two weeks.
How long have you been living here?

note: Learners negate with no + gerund; the absence form is sin + infinitive. Frame: llevar + time + gerund; llevar + time + sin + infinitive

title: si tuviera or si hubiera tenido?
en: If I had money, I'd travel.

forms.en: If I had money, I'd travel.

forms.es: Si hubiera tenido plata, habría viajado.
forms.en: If I'd had money, I would have travelled.

title: Good at it or able to: se me da bien, soy capaz de, soy bueno para

forms.es: Soy capaz de correr diez kilómetros.
forms.en: I'm able to run ten kilometres.

forms.es: No fui capaz de decirle la verdad.
forms.en: I wasn't able to tell him the truth.

note: Natural aptitude vs one specific act vs general skill.

title: aunque llueve or aunque llueva?
en: Although it's raining, I'm going out.

forms.en: Although it's raining, I'm going out.
Even if it rains, I'll go out.

title: Naming no one or naming you: habría que vs deberías
A hunch or a doubt: tengo la impresión de que + indicativo vs no estoy seguro de que + subjuntivo
es: Tengo la impresión de que no vendrá.
en: I have a feeling he won't come.

forms.es: Tengo la impresión de que no vendrá.
forms.en: I have a feeling he won't come.

forms.es: No estoy seguro de que venga.

note: Mood follows commitment: the hunch asserts, the doubt doesn't.

title: Assertive or tentative opinion: a mi modo de ver vs yo diría que
es: A mi modo de ver, es la mejor opción.
en: The way I see it, it's the best option.

forms.es: A mi modo de ver, es la mejor opción.
forms.en: The way I see it, it's the best option.

forms.es: Yo diría que es la mejor opción.
forms.en: I'd say it's the best option.

title: Mientras: "while" vs "as long as"
en: While you cook, I'll set the table.

forms.en: While you cook, I'll set the table.

forms.es: Mientras cocines tú, yo lavo los platos.
forms.en: As long as you cook, I'll do the washing-up.

note: Indicative = time; subjunctive = condition.

title: Half-remembering vs remembering: me suena vs me acuerdo

forms.es: Me acuerdo perfectamente de su cara.

note: Also mixes gustar-type and reflexive grammar.

title: After vs on: tras firmar vs al firmar

forms.es: Al firmar, se dio cuenta del error.
forms.en: As he signed, he noticed the mistake.

note: tras = después de (sequence); al = at the moment of / when.

title: So tired that or tired enough to: tan cansado que, tan cansado como para
es: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.
en: I was so tired I fell asleep.

forms.es: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.
forms.en: I was so tired I fell asleep.

forms.es: No estaba tan cansado como para dormirme.
forms.en: I wasn't tired enough to fall asleep.

note: que = a real result; como para = a threshold, often negated.

title: Which (the whole idea) vs which (a noun): lo que vs el que
es: No vino, lo que me molestó.
en: He didn't come, which annoyed me.

forms.es: No vino, lo que me molestó.
forms.en: He didn't come, which annoyed me.

forms.es: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
forms.en: The house I live in is old.

note: Clause antecedent → lo que/lo cual; noun antecedent → el/la que.

title: Whose action: no recuerdo haber dicho eso vs no recuerdo que él dijera eso

forms.es: No recuerdo que él dijera eso.
forms.en: I don't remember him saying that.

note: Same subject → infinitive; different subject → que + subjunctive.

title: Sorry for them or sorry for what I did: siento que… vs siento no haber…
note: Using que + subjunctive for your own action is the common slip.

title: Ending up doing or going as far as: acabó por, llegó a

forms.en: He even came to hate it.

note: Both 'end-state' periphrases; learners swap them.

title: Sure because I feel it vs sure because I know it
en: I could swear I saw him yesterday.

forms.en: I could swear I saw him yesterday.

forms.es: No me cabe duda de que vendrá.
forms.en: I have no doubt he'll come.
I know for a fact that he paid.

title: The imperfect that isn't past: surprise, politeness or hearsay?

forms.es: Venía a preguntar si tenían habitaciones.
forms.en: I was coming to ask if you had any rooms.
Ernesto was arriving tomorrow, wasn't he?

note: Mixed recognition practice: what is the speaker doing with the imperfect?

title: A hunch vs a formal possibility
en: If you ask me, he's not coming.

forms.en: If you ask me, he's not coming.

forms.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que no venga.
forms.en: There's a possibility that he won't come.

note: Register and mood: para mí que + indic; cabe la posibilidad de que + subj.

title: Rephrasing vs setting aside
es: Es mañana, es decir, el sábado.

forms.es: Es mañana, es decir, el sábado.

forms.en: There are three, or rather, four.

forms.es: Puede que tengas razón; en cualquier caso, hay que decidir hoy.
forms.en: You may be right; in any case, we have to decide today.

note: Choosing the wrong class misreports your intention.

title: Thanks in advance or booking in advance: de antemano, con antelación
note: De antemano = knowing/thanking beforehand; con antelación = acting with margin before a deadline.

title: Agreeing partly vs fully
es: No te falta razón, ahora bien, hay que pensar en el costo.
en: You've got a point; that said, we need to think about the cost.

forms.es: No te falta razón, ahora bien, hay que pensar en el costo.
forms.en: You've got a point; that said, we need to think about the cost.

forms.es: Coincido contigo en que hay que cambiar el plan.
forms.en: I agree with you that we need to change the plan.

title: Turning a blind eye or overlooking: hacer la vista gorda, pasar por alto
Settling for or having no choice: conformarse con, no quedar más remedio

forms.es: No me quedó más remedio que irme.
forms.en: I had no choice but to leave.

note: Different structures (con + noun vs que + inf) for overlapping resignation meanings.

title: At the same time as or as (progressively): al tiempo que, a medida que
es: Sube la producción al tiempo que cae la demanda.

forms.es: Sube la producción al tiempo que cae la demanda.
A medida que avanza la tarde, baja la temperatura.
forms.en: As the afternoon goes on, the temperature drops.

note: Simultaneous (often contrasting) facts vs parallel progression.

title: Blunt order vs ceremonious request

forms.en: Would you be so kind as to be quiet?

note: Same content, opposite ends of the ladder; register-matching practice.

title: Cualquier día vs un día cualquiera
note: Before the noun: any (cualquier); after: ordinary (cualquiera).
